title: 2016 HMMT November Team Problem 1
statement: Two circles centered at \(O_{1}\) and \(O_{2}\) have radii 2 and 3 and are externally tangent at \(P\). The common external tangent of the two circles intersects the line \(O_{1} O_{2}\) at \(Q\). What is the length of \(P Q\) ?

solutions.text:
Answer: 12
Let the common external tangent intersect the circles centered at \(O_{1}, O_{2}\) at \(X, Y\) respectively. Then \(\frac{O_{2} Q}{O_{1} Q}=\frac{O Y}{O X}=\frac{3}{2}\), so \(\frac{O_{1} O_{2}}{O_{1} Q}=\frac{O_{2} Q-O_{1} Q}{O_{1} Q}=\frac{1}{2}\). Since \(O_{1} O_{2}=2+3=5, O_{1} Q=10\) and hence \(P Q=O_{1} Q+O_{1} P=12\).
